newsitem.title: UK: Fleming boosts profits despite lower Asian return.
newsitem.headline: Fleming boosts profits despite lower Asian return.

text.p: British independent investment bank Robert Fleming on Thursday reported a 25 percent rise in annual profits and said the new financial year had got off to a good start.
It made pre-tax profits for the year to March 31 of 167.6 million pounds ($279 million), up from the previous year's 133.5 million pounds. It also increased its total dividend 14 percent to 25 pence.
But the contribution from Jardine Fleming, the group's Asian troubled joint venture with Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd, fell from 50.5 million pounds to 37.7 million pounds.

"Asia has had a difficult year but the rest of it did extremely well. Indeed, the non-Asian business is at a record level in terms of profits for the year," Fleming's chief executive William Garrett told Reuters.

Garrett said there was "quite a lot of development expenditure going on in the East", but he did not quantify this and could not say when Jardine Fleming might return to its previous levels of profitability.
He said the regulatory problems at Jardine Fleming had been put behind it and there had been a dramatic improvement in investment performance now the distractions were over.
Last August, Jardine Fleming revealed a five-month probe by British and Hong Kong regulators into irregular trades by a former senior fund manager at Jardine Fleming Investment Management.
This resulted in hefty fines and voluntary compensation of nearly $20 million to clients. Regulators also withdrew the authorisation of Jardine Fleming's London-based fund company.
But Garrett was upbeat about prospects in Asia.
"Asia, we continue to believe, will be a growth area in the future again, but with a slightly different nuance. As the Asian economies mature there will be different opportunities for us."
"In the context of the group...Jardine Fleming is a relatively small part this year and the rest of business has grown spectacularly," he added.

Flemings said its asset management operations had reported a significant rise in profitability, helped by contributions from Rowe Price-Fleming International, Fleming Investment Management, Save & Prosper and its European fund distribution division.

A strong performance from its European operations had boosed the firm's securities business while investmnet banking had "a busy and profitable year" and banking had another record year, with a 25 percent increase in retail deposits.

Garrett said it was too early to say if Flemings would match the 25 percent increase in pre-tax profits in the current year, and while he hoped to show another increase, it would depend on market conditions over the period.

He said that on the whole there were now no areas where he felt Flemings ought to be represented. Based around its core activities, it had built up a strong network of offices and joint ventures around the world, he said.
"From here our head count is not likely to grow very dramatically," he said, adding that acquisitions were not generally the firm's style and it could enter instead into further joint ventures.
"In Brazil, for instance, we might very well have a joint venture there before the end of the year," he said. This tactic worked well and fitted well with local characteristics and conditions.
While rumours of consolidation in the industry circulate daily, Flemings will remain independent and had not been approached by competitors trying to take over the privately-owned group.
"We are very pleased to be independent. We like to be independent, the (Fleming) family likes us to be independent, so we are all pointing in the same direction."
($ = 0.601 British Pounds)
